claim: The Affimer scaffold (Adhiron) has a thermal stability with Tm = 101°C
source: The Adhiron scaffold is a synthetic protein originally based on a cystatin consensus sequence and displays remarkable thermal stability (Tm = 101°C) (Tiede et al., 2014).
evidence: The thermal stability value is cited from a previous publication (Tiede et al., 2014)

claim: The Affimer scaffold is related in structure to a scaffold engineered from human stefin A
source: It is related in structure to a previously reported scaffold engineered from human stefin A (Stadler et al., 2011).
evidence: This relationship is supported by citation to Stadler et al., 2011

claim: The Affimer scaffold crystal structure was solved at 1.75 Å resolution
source: X-ray crystal structure of Affimer scaffold (PDB ID no. 4N6T) at 1.75 A resolution.
evidence: The resolution is stated in the figure caption and the structure is deposited in PDB

claim: Up to 75% of commercially available antibodies have either not been validated, show a low level of validation or simply do not perform adequately in certain applications
source: While there are over 500,000 different antibodies on the market, it has been reported that up to 75% have either not been validated, show a low level of validation or simply do not perform adequately in certain applications (Berglund et al., 2008).
evidence: This statistic is cited from Berglund et al., 2008

claim: The human genome encodes some 120 SH2 domains found in 111 proteins
source: The human genome encodes some 120 SH2 domains found in 111 proteins (Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: This information is cited from Liu et al., 2011

claim: Affimers were successfully isolated against nine SH2 domains with 50-100% of clones binding to target
source: From each screen we randomly selected phagemid clones and by phage ELISA confirmed that Affimers had been selected against each of the nine SH2 domains. The proportion of clones that bound to each target, but not to the control, was between 50% and 100% with an average of 87.6%.
evidence: The binding success rates are reported from experimental phage ELISA data

claim: Grb2, 7, and 10 SH2 domain binding Affimers showed specific binding without cross-reactivity to other Grb family members
source: Initially, the Grb2, 7, 10 and 14 SH2 domain binding Affimers were tested for cross-reactivity against the other Grb family members, and showed specific binding to the Grb SH2 domain, with the exception of Grb14 Affimers which showed weak cross-reactivity with Grb7 and Grb10 proteins but not Grb2.
evidence: Specificity is demonstrated by phage ELISA data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Grb14 Affimers showed weak cross-reactivity with Grb7 and Grb10 proteins but not Grb2
source: Initially, the Grb2, 7, 10 and 14 SH2 domain binding Affimers were tested for cross-reactivity against the other Grb family members, and showed specific binding to the Grb SH2 domain, with the exception of Grb14 Affimers which showed weak cross-reactivity with Grb7 and Grb10 proteins but not Grb2.
evidence: Cross-reactivity is shown in phage ELISA data in Figure 2A

claim: The level of pairwise sequence homology between Grb7, 10 and 14 is between 65–72%
source: The level of pairwise sequence homology between Grb7, 10 and 14 is between 65–72% (Daly, 1998).
evidence: The sequence homology values are cited from Daly, 1998

claim: Five Grb2-binding Affimers successfully pulled down endogenous Grb2 from U2OS cell lysates
source: All five reagents successfully pulled-down Grb2 whereas a yeast SUMO-binding control Affimer (Tiede et al., 2014) was unable to pull down Grb2.
evidence: Pull-down success is demonstrated by Western blot in Figure 2B

claim: A yeast SUMO-binding control Affimer was unable to pull down Grb2
source: All five reagents successfully pulled-down Grb2 whereas a yeast SUMO-binding control Affimer (Tiede et al., 2014) was unable to pull down Grb2.
evidence: Negative control result is shown in Western blot in Figure 2B

claim: The N-terminal SH2 domains of p85α, p85β and p55γ variants have 83-90% pairwise sequence identity
source: Despite a high degree of sequence identity (pairwise between 83–90%) a number of p85α-specific Affimers were isolated (e.g., clones 1 and 2; Figure 2C).
evidence: The sequence identity values are stated in the text describing the experimental results

claim: p85α-specific Affimers were isolated despite high sequence identity between p85 isoforms
source: Despite a high degree of sequence identity (pairwise between 83–90%) a number of p85α-specific Affimers were isolated (e.g., clones 1 and 2; Figure 2C).
evidence: Specificity is demonstrated by phage ELISA data in Figure 2C

claim: Some Affimers recognized the α and γ but not β p85 N-terminal SH2 domains
source: Affimers that recognised the α and γ but not β domain were also isolated (clones 3 and 23).
evidence: Binding specificity is shown in phage ELISA data in Figure 2C

claim: None of the p85 N-terminal SH2 domain Affimers bound to any of the C-terminal p85/p55 SH2 domains
source: None of these Affimers bound to any of the C-terminal p85/p55 SH2 domains.
evidence: Lack of binding to C-terminal domains is shown in phage ELISA data in Figure 2C

claim: p85 SH2 domain-specific Affimers expressed in NIH 3T3 cells bound to endogenous p85 protein
source: The p85 SH2 domain-specific Affimers were expressed in NIH 3T3 cells and their ability to bind to endogenous p85 protein was assessed by co-immunopreciptation assays, in which p85α was pulled-down. The p85α antibody also pulled down both p110α and the FLAG-tagged Affimers (Figure 2D).
evidence: Binding to endogenous protein is demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation Western blot in Figure 2D

claim: The p85 SH2 domain Affimers did not disrupt the p85/p110 overall complex
source: In addition the Affimers did not disrupt the p85/p110 overall complex in which p85 interacts with p110 via three domains, with the SH2 domain regulating activity via binding p110 (Vivanco and Sawyers, 2002).
evidence: The maintenance of the complex is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data and cited mechanism from Vivanco and Sawyers, 2002

claim: Five of six p85 N-terminal SH2 domain Affimers mediated an increase in AKT phosphorylation
source: Five of the six Affimer proteins mediated an increase in AKT phosphorylation (Figure 2E) demonstrating that they inhibit the interaction between the N-terminal p85 SH2 domain and p110, but importantly do not block p85-p110 complex formation.
evidence: AKT phosphorylation increase is shown by Western blot and quantification in Figure 2E

claim: siRNA inhibition of p85α alone had little effect on cells, but p85 and p110 both had to be eliminated to produce a phenotype and an effect on AKT phosphorylation
source: This supports a report that siRNA inhibition of p85α alone had little effect on cells, but that p85 and p110 both had to be eliminated to produce a phenotype and an effect on AKT phosphorylation (Kim et al., 2005).
evidence: This finding is cited from Kim et al., 2005

claim: VEGFR2 is a key molecule that regulates many aspects of vascular physiology and blood vessel formation especially angiogenesis
source: In this context, VEGFR2 is a key molecule that regulates many aspects of vascular physiology and blood vessel formation especially angiogenesis and is associated with tumour neovascularisation (Kofler and Simons, 2015).
evidence: This role of VEGFR2 is cited from Kofler and Simons, 2015

claim: VEGFR2 screening yielded positive clones representing only two distinct sequences
source: In this case DNA sequence analysis revealed that the positive clones represented only two distinct sequences.
evidence: This is reported from DNA sequencing analysis of positive clones

claim: VEGFR2 Affimer A9 has an affinity of 41 ± 17 nM
source: The affinities for VEGFR2 of representative Affimer proteins, A9 and B8, were determined by SPR to be 41 ± 17 nM and 240 ± 124 nM, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Affinity was measured by SPR as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: VEGFR2 Affimer B8 has an affinity of 240 ± 124 nM
source: The affinities for VEGFR2 of representative Affimer proteins, A9 and B8, were determined by SPR to be 41 ± 17 nM and 240 ± 124 nM, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Affinity was measured by SPR as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: The efficiency of Affimer labelling with biotin was determined to be 80–90% by mass spectrometry
source: The efficiency of Affimer labelling with biotin was determined to be 80–90% by mass spectrometry (data not shown).
evidence: Labeling efficiency was measured by mass spectrometry

claim: VEGFR2 Affimers showed the same staining pattern as anti-VEGFR2 antibodies in tissue sections
source: The Affimer reagents showed exactly the same staining pattern as the antibodies, with VEGFR2 staining being predominantly localised in the epithelial cells and with more intense staining at the cell membrane (Figure 3B; see arrows).
evidence: Staining patterns are compared in immunohistochemistry images in Figure 3B

claim: VEGFR2 Affimer staining developed more quickly than antibody staining
source: In this case, the staining developed more quickly for the Affimer binders than for the antibody indicating a higher sensitivity of staining.
evidence: This observation is reported from the immunohistochemistry experiments

claim: VEGFR2 Affimer B8 inhibited VEGF-dependent tubule length and branch point formation in a tubulogenesis assay
source: By contrast, the inhibitory effect of Affimer B8 could be measured within just 30 min of treatment and also led to a decrease in VEGF-dependent tubule length and branch point formation in a tubulogenesis assay (Figure 3C).
evidence: Inhibition is demonstrated by tubulogenesis assay data in Figure 3C

claim: VEGFR2 Affimer B8 inhibited VEGF-dependent phosphorylation of VEGFR2 and downstream signalling mediators PLCg1, AKT, ERK, p38 and eNOS
source: Consistent with the effects on tubulogenesis, Affimer B8 also inhibited VEGF-dependent phosphorylation of VEGFR2 and downstream signalling, with decreased activation of cell signalling mediators PLCg1, AKT, ERK, p38 and eNOS (n = 3; Figure 3D).
evidence: Inhibition of signaling is shown by Western blot in Figure 3D

claim: Control Affimers had no effect on VEGFR2 signalling
source: By contrast control Affimers had no effect on signalling.
evidence: This is stated as a control result from the signaling experiments

claim: Thirteen unique Affimer clones were identified from 24 positive clones against TRPV1 peptide
source: Thirteen unique Affimer clones were identified from 24 positive clones identified by phage ELISA of 96 randomly selected colonies from the phage library screen (Figure 4A).
evidence: Clone identification is reported from phage ELISA screening shown in Figure 4A

claim: None of the 13 TRPV1 binders showed cross-reactivity to a peptide derived from the pore region of Nav1.7
source: None of the 13 binders showed cross-reactivity to a distinct peptide derived from the pore region of a voltage-gated sodium channel, Nav1.7.
evidence: Specificity is reported from cross-reactivity testing

claim: TRPV1 Affimer 2 showed no staining of TRPV1-negative U2-OS control cells
source: Affimer 2 showed no staining of TRPV1-negative U2-OS control cells.
evidence: Negative control result is reported from affinity-fluorescence experiments

claim: Six TRPV1 Affimers showed significant enhancement of TRPV1 activation upon treatment with capsaicin
source: While no direct modulation was observed six Affimers showed significant enhancement of TRPV1 activation upon treatment with the agonist capsaicin (Figure 4D) compared with cells treated with capsaicin alone.
evidence: Enhancement is demonstrated by calcium uptake assay data in Figure 4D

claim: The small molecule compound MRS1477 led to a three-fold increase in capsaicin activation of TRPV1 when applied at low micromolar concentrations
source: The compound (MRS1477) was hypothesised to interact with the pore-forming region of TRPV1, leading to a three-fold increase in capsaicin activation when applied at low micromolar concentrations – an effect similar to that reported here for some of the Affimers.
evidence: This effect is cited from previous research (Kaszas et al., 2012)

claim: Tenascin C is frequently up-regulated in cancer tissues and associated with metastasis
source: Tenascin C (TNC) is an extracellular matrix protein that is abundant during early development, is expressed at low levels in adult tissues and is frequently up-regulated in cancer tissues and associated with metastasis (Minn et al., 2005; Oskarsson et al., 2011) and poor patient outcomes (Lowy and Oskarsson, 2015).
evidence: This association is cited from Minn et al., 2005 and Oskarsson et al., 2011

claim: Tenascin C is associated with poor patient outcomes
source: Tenascin C (TNC) is an extracellular matrix protein that is abundant during early development, is expressed at low levels in adult tissues and is frequently up-regulated in cancer tissues and associated with metastasis (Minn et al., 2005; Oskarsson et al., 2011) and poor patient outcomes (Lowy and Oskarsson, 2015).
evidence: This association is cited from Lowy and Oskarsson, 2015

claim: One TNC Affimer protein has high affinity for TNC with KD = 5.7 ± 2.8 nM
source: One Affimer protein with high affinity for TNC (KD = 5.7 ± 2.8 nM by SPR – sup Figure 2) was used in subsequent assays.
evidence: Affinity was measured by SPR

claim: TNC Affimer staining patterns were similar to those obtained with TNC antibody in tissue sections
source: Staining patterns with C-terminally biotinylated TNC Affimer were similar to those obtained with the TNC antibody (Figure 5B).
evidence: Staining patterns are compared in immunohistochemistry images in Figure 5B

claim: GFP Affimer showed a significant decrease in kidney fluorescence from 24 to 48 hr post-injection (p=0.04)
source: However, compared to the TNC Affimer this clearance was faster for the GFP Affimer as it showed a significant decrease (p=0.04) in fluorescence from 24 to 48 hr post-injection (fold change 9.23 ± 3.10 at 24 hr to 2.98 ± 0.77 at 48 hr; Figure 5D).
evidence: Clearance is quantified from ex vivo imaging data in Figure 5D

claim: TNC Affimer signal at 24 hr post-injection was significantly higher (p=0.02) in tumours compared with the control GFP Affimer group
source: The TNC Affimer signal at 24 hr post-injection was significantly higher (p=0.02) in tumours (6.26 ± 1.62) compared with the control GFP Affimer group (2.32 ± 0.61) suggesting that the TNC Affimer accumulated in the TNC expressing tumour.
evidence: Tumor accumulation is quantified from ex vivo imaging data in Figure 5D

claim: The ratio of anti-TNC Affimer binders in tumour compared to the spleen was >6 at 24 hr
source: In addition, the ratio of anti-TNC Affimer binders in tumour compared to the spleen, for example, was >6 at 24 hr (Figure 5D); in contrast, anti-TNC antibodies took 2 days to reach a tumour/spleen ratio of 5, although this did improve to 20–30 at day 10 (De Santis et al., 2006).
evidence: Tumor-to-spleen ratio is calculated from ex vivo imaging data in Figure 5D

claim: Anti-TNC antibodies took 2 days to reach a tumour/spleen ratio of 5, which improved to 20–30 at day 10
source: In addition, the ratio of anti-TNC Affimer binders in tumour compared to the spleen, for example, was >6 at 24 hr (Figure 5D); in contrast, anti-TNC antibodies took 2 days to reach a tumour/spleen ratio of 5, although this did improve to 20–30 at day 10 (De Santis et al., 2006).
evidence: This antibody performance is cited from De Santis et al., 2006

claim: HVT UL49 Affimers were specific for HVT and did not bind to MDV (RB1B) or DEV proteins
source: Phage ELISA, affinity-fluorescence and in-cell Western confirmed that the selected Affimers were specific for HTV recombinant proteins as well as their ability to specifically stain the target protein in primary Chicken Embryonic Fibroblasts (CEFs) containing bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) clones of MDV-1 (RB1B), HVT or DEV (strain 2085) (Figure 6A,B and C).
evidence: Specificity is demonstrated by phage ELISA, affinity-fluorescence and in-cell Western in Figures 6A, B and C

claim: The affinity of anti HVT UL49 Affimers was in the low nM range, with KD values of 1.5 nM to 7.5 nM with a mean of 3.3 nM for eight clones tested
source: The affinity of anti HVT UL49 Affimers was in the low nM range, KD values of 1.5 nM to 7.5 nM with a mean 3.3 nM, for the eight clones tested (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Affinities were measured and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: Anti-HVT UL49 Affimers detected cytoplasmic foci in infected cells consistent with sites of HVT secondary viral envelopment
source: Compared with low background staining with the streptavidin only control (SA only) there are pronounced cytoplasmic foci detected by Affimers in infected cells. These foci are consistent with data from the related alphaherpesvirus MDV (Denesvre et al., 2007; Rémy et al., 2013) or the model alphaherpesviruses Herpes Simplex type 1 (HSV-1) (Stylianou et al., 2009) and Pseudorabies virus (PrV) (del Rio et al., 2002) and likely indicate the cytoplasmic sites of HVT secondary viral envelopment.
evidence: Foci are observed in affinity-fluorescence images in Figure 6C and compared to literature on related viruses

claim: HER4 Affimer binding to CHO cells expressing HER4 increases from 5 nM to 100 nM as determined by membrane signal intensity
source: When HER4 is over-expressed in CHO cells the Affimer showed increasing binding at concentrations from 5 nM to 100 nM, as determined by membrane signal intensity from confocal microscopy images, while in MCF7 cells that express physiological levels of HER4 binding increases from 10 to 200 nM Affimer (Figure 7B).
evidence: Binding is quantified from confocal microscopy images in Figure 7B

claim: HER4 Affimer binding to MCF7 cells expressing physiological levels of HER4 increases from 10 to 200 nM
source: When HER4 is over-expressed in CHO cells the Affimer showed increasing binding at concentrations from 5 nM to 100 nM, as determined by membrane signal intensity from confocal microscopy images, while in MCF7 cells that express physiological levels of HER4 binding increases from 10 to 200 nM Affimer (Figure 7B).
evidence: Binding is quantified from confocal microscopy images in Figure 7B

claim: dSTORM imaging of HER4 with Affimer-Alexa 647 achieved a localisation precision of ca. 25 nm
source: The corresponding direct Stochastic Optical Reconstruction Microscopy (dSTORM) image (Figure 7C – bottom) has a localisation precision of ca. 25 nm.
evidence: Localization precision is stated for the dSTORM image in Figure 7C

claim: Bayesian cluster analysis of HER4 dSTORM images shows the most prevalent cluster size is between 8.1 and 12 nm in radius
source: A Bayesian cluster analysis (Griffié et al., 2016) of the dSTORM image shows that the most prevalent cluster size of HER4 oligomers is between 8.1 and 12 nm in radius.
evidence: Cluster size is determined by Bayesian analysis of dSTORM data shown in Figure 7C

claim: The most prevalent number of HER4 molecules in a cluster is between 4 to 8
source: This corresponds with the most prevalent number of HER4 molecules in a cluster being between 4 to 8.
evidence: Molecule number is determined from cluster analysis of dSTORM data shown in Figure 7C

claim: HER4 forms oligomers as large as those previously found in EGFR
source: These data show that HER4 forms oligomers as large as those previously found in EGFR. (Needham et al., 2016)
evidence: This comparison is made based on the cluster analysis data and cited from Needham et al., 2016

claim: There is an immobile or scarcely mobile population of HER4 receptors on MCF7 cells, associated with a tail of highly mobile molecules
source: The data show that there is an immobile, or scarcely mobile, population of HER4 receptors on MCF7 cells, associated with a tail of highly mobile molecules (Figure 7D, left panel).
evidence: Mobility is determined from single-particle tracking data shown in Figure 7D

claim: Unlike EGFR, the diffusion of HER4 is not confined on the timescales investigated
source: The near straight slope of the MSD plot indicates that, unlike EGFR (Needham et al., 2016; Zanetti-Domingues et al., 2012), the diffusion of HER4 is not confined on the timescales investigated (Figure 7D, right panel).
evidence: Diffusion behavior is determined from MSD analysis in Figure 7D and compared to EGFR from cited studies

claim: The tubulin Affimer labels interphase microtubules in a similar way to a widely-used antibody
source: The Affimer we selected labels interphase microtubules in a similar way to a widely-used antibody (Figure 8A).
evidence: Labeling is compared in confocal images in Figure 8A

claim: In mitotic cells, the tubulin Affimer labels the spindle but not astral microtubules
source: However, in mitotic cells, the Affimer labels the spindle but not astral microtubules (Figure 8A) likely reflecting the fact that the antibody recognises tyrosinated microtubules unlike the Affimer.
evidence: Differential labeling is shown in confocal images in Figure 8A

claim: The tubulin Affimer is able to label the central region of the cytokinetic furrow where microtubules are very densely packed
source: Interestingly, the Affimer is able to label the central region of the cytokinetic furrow (Figure 8A), in which microtubules are very densely packed.
evidence: Labeling of the cytokinetic furrow is shown in confocal images in Figure 8A

claim: Antibodies are usually excluded from the central region of the cytokinetic furrow
source: Antibodies are usually excluded from this region so analysis of this feature has been problematic (Hu et al., 2012).
evidence: This limitation of antibodies is cited from Hu et al., 2012

claim: Average microtubule profiles were substantially narrower with Affimer labelling (47 ± 11 nm) than with primary antibody labelling (73 ± 10 nm) as measured by FWHM
source: While localisation density may not be fully optimised in these samples (Huang et al., 2008) the average microtubule profiles were substantially narrower with Affimer labelling (47 ± 11 nm) than with primary antibody labelling (73 ± 10 nm) (FWHM, mean ± s.d.) and should allow further elucidation of tubulin structures that have previously not been solved.
evidence: Profile widths are measured from dSTORM images and quantified in Figure 8D

claim: Within variable loop 1 of TNT Affimers it was possible to define a short consensus sequence implying a common binding mode
source: Of the 32 clones tested 14 distinct sequences were identified, some containing only variable region 1 which indicates selection from a small sub-population of the original phage display library. Within variable loop 1 it was possible to define a short consensus sequence implying a common binding mode.
evidence: Consensus sequence is identified from DNA sequencing analysis of selected clones

claim: All four TNT Affimers showed binding to the original TNBS-conjugate and to TNT
source: Four Affimer proteins were purified and tested for binding to TNT and various dinitrotoluenes (DNT; Figure 9A) by competition ELISA (Figure 9C). All four Affimers showed binding to the original TNBS-conjugate and to TNT, but differed in their specificity for the DNTs.
evidence: Binding is demonstrated by competition ELISA data in Figure 9C

claim: TNT Affimer 4 showed a higher level of specificity for TNT than any of the DNTs
source: Affimer 4, a VR1 only Affimer, showed a higher level of specificity for TNT than any of the DNTs.
evidence: Specificity is demonstrated by competition ELISA data in Figure 9C

claim: TNT Affimer 3 binds to TNT and provides discrimination between 2,4-DNT and the other two DNTs
source: By contrast, Affimer 3 binds to TNT and also provides discrimination between 2,4-DNT and the other two DNT's.
evidence: Discrimination is demonstrated by competition ELISA data in Figure 9C

claim: The BioScreening Technology Group (BSTG) has performed more than 350 successful screens to date
source: We now report on some of the outcomes of the more than 350 successful screens performed by the BSTG to date, and suggest that access to this and similar facilities (eg High Throughput Binder Selection facility at the University of Zurich) should deliver the tools needed to complement antibodies in the dissection of biological functions of individual proteins and protein isoforms.
evidence: This number is stated as a summary of the BSTG's work

claim: Each Affimer screening regime consisting of three panning rounds of phage display and phage ELISA was normally completed in 12 days
source: Typically each screening regime, consisting normally of three panning rounds of phage display and phage ELISA, was normally completed in 12 days.
evidence: This timeline is reported from the screening protocol

claim: Affimer selection is much faster than antibody and nanobody production techniques that involve animal inoculation
source: Thus Affimer selection, as with other alternative protein or antibody fragment selection approaches that use phage display or other in vitro selection, is much faster than antibody and nanobody production techniques that involve animal inoculation.
evidence: This comparison is based on the reported 12-day timeline for Affimer selection

claim: Of the 36 Affimers reported, an average yield of 83.3 mg/L (1.5–188 mg/L) culture was achieved with purity greater than 95% following a single immobilised metal affinity step
source: Of the 36 Affimers reported on here an average yield of 83.3 mg/L (1.5–188 mg/L) culture was achieved with a purity of greater than 95% following a single immobilised metal affinity step.
evidence: Yield and purity are reported from protein purification data

claim: Without automation the phage display platform allows an individual to screen up to 24 targets simultaneously
source: Without automation the phage display platform allows an individual to screen up to 24 targets simultaneously.
evidence: This capacity is stated based on the manual screening protocol

claim: Affimer technology is commercially available through Avacta Life Sciences or for academic collaborations through the University of Leeds
source: Affimer technology is commercially available through Avacta Life Sciences or for academic collaborations through the University of Leeds.
evidence: This availability is stated in the discussion

claim: The Affimer library can be synthesised as described by Tiede et al. (2014) and screened in individual laboratories
source: Alternatively, the library can be synthesised as described by Tiede et al. (2014) and screened in individual laboratories, making this technology immediately accessible to the scientific community.
evidence: This accessibility is stated with reference to the synthesis protocol from Tiede et al., 2014
